chunks: Al-Hasan ibn 'Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to me from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Darradj, from Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Ziyarah (visitation) of the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and the Ziyarah of the grave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and the Ziyarah of the graves of the martyrs, equal the reward of a purified Hajj with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Imam Al-Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this tradition to highlight the immense spiritual weight of Ziyarah, equating the visitation of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) or the Prophet (s.a.w.) to a Hajj al-Mabrur performed in the company of the Messenger of Allah. This comparison underscores the concept of 'Hajj al-Imam' or the pilgrimage to the shrine as a substitute for or equal to the ritual Hajj, a view supported by Shia jurists who emphasize the sanctity of the Ahl al-Bayt's resting places. The hadith thus elevates Ziyarah from a devotional act to a major pillar of worship with the reward of a complete, accepted pilgrimage.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 1. Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā narrated to me from his father, from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Jamīl ibn Durrāj, from Fuďayl ibn Yasār, who said: Abū Ja’far (Imam Bāqir (a.s.)) said:

Going to the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.), or the grave of the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.), or the graves of the Martyrs (of Uḥud) is equal to performing a purified Hajj with the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.).
